key_parts.system:
You write the plain-language line for a rental housing law app. The app always shows the quoted law, its citation and "Not legal advice." next to your sentence.

For each rule you get its quoted text (the only source of law you may use) and a few structured fields. Write two sentences:
- answer_tenant: addressed to a tenant ("you" = the tenant).
- answer_owner: addressed to the landlord or property owner ("you" = the owner).

Rules for every sentence:
1. One sentence, at most 20 words, containing "you" or "your".
2. Start with the answer itself (e.g. "Your landlord must...", "You must...", "You can..."). No preamble such as "Under this law", "This rule" or "According to".
3. Use only what the quoted text says. Add no facts, conditions, deadlines or remedies that are not in it. If the quote is too thin to say anything useful (for example only a bill title), return null for that sentence.
4. Numbers, dates, percentages and dollar amounts: copy them exactly as they appear in the quote or key_value. Never compute, convert, round or combine them. If unsure, leave the number out.
5. Owner sentences state obligations or prohibitions only. Never mention exemptions, exceptions, how a rule might not apply, or any way to avoid, get around or work around a rule. Tenant sentences state rights and protections, also without exemption talk.
6. Status: "pending" means a bill or proposal that is not law, so say it is proposed and would apply only if enacted; "not_yet_effective" means enacted but not yet in effect, so say it is not in effect yet (no date unless the quote states it); "in_force" is present tense.
7. Do not name the jurisdiction or the citation; the app shows them. Do not give legal advice, promise outcomes or say anyone is compliant.

Return JSON with one entry per rule id given, in the same order.

input.title: Security deposit held in separate interest-bearing account
input.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property.

input.title: Interest on security deposits
input.key_value: five per cent per year, or lesser amount received from the bank
input.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

input.title: Return of security deposit and permitted deductions
input.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;

input.title: Security deposit return and forfeiture of right to retain
input.key_value: Return within thirty days after termination of the tenancy
input.quoted_span: (e) fails to return to the tenant the security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled after deducting therefrom any sums in accordance with the provisions of this section, together with any interest thereon, within thirty days after termination of the tenancy.

input.title: Transfer of last month's rent advance to successor in interest
input.key_value: Written notice within forty-five days from the date of transfer
input.quoted_span: The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such rental advance that such rental advance was so credited, and that such successor has assumed responsibility therefor pursuant to the foregoing provision.

input.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
input.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for:

input.title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
input.key_value: $50, adjusted annually in direct proportion to the percent change in the Consumer Price Index (only if the change is greater than zero)
input.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.

input.title: Good cause required for non-renewal of residential leases (Anti-Eviction Act)
input.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

input.title: No eviction solely because the lease term ended
input.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended.

input.title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
input.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

input.title: Eviction for failure to pay rent
input.key_value: 14-day notice for federally subsidized housing; no notice otherwise
input.quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may immediately take legal action to have the tenant evicted. The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.

input.title: Nonpayment eviction bar when tenant pays landlord-owed utilities
input.quoted_span: Note: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent, if the tenant used the unpaid portion of rent to continue utility services to the rental premises after receiving notice that the services were in danger of being discontinued, and if the landlord was responsible for the payment of those utility services and did not make the payments required to retain the us e of those services.

answers.answer_tenant: Your landlord must hold your security deposit in a separate, interest-bearing bank account located within the commonwealth.
answers.answer_owner: You must hold any security deposit you receive in a separate, interest-bearing bank account located within the commonwealth.

answers.answer_owner: You must pay the tenant interest at five per cent per year, or any lesser amount the bank paid.

answers.answer_owner: You must return the tenant's security deposit or any balance within thirty days after the tenancy ends.

answers.answer_owner: You must return the tenant's deposit balance, together with any interest, within thirty days after the tenancy ends.

answers.answer_owner: You, as successor, must notify the tenant within forty-five days from the transfer date that their rental advance was credited.

answers.answer_owner: You must not require an application or similar fee exceeding $50 to apply to lease a residential rental property.

answers.answer_owner: You may not fail to renew a residential lease, written or oral, unless you have good cause.

answers.answer_owner: You cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended.

answers.answer_tenant: Your landlord cannot evict you or fail to renew your lease, written or oral, without good cause.
